contentBlocks.title: Identity Verification Failed — How to Fix It
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA status shows 'Identity Verification Failed or Pending' — your grant is on hold until your identity is confirmed. Learn how to complete facial verification, what to do if Home Affairs records don't match, and how to resolve this quickly.

contentBlocks.text: Identity Verification Failed/Pending — What It Means

The 'Identity Verification Failed' or 'Identity Verification Pending' status means SASSA could not confirm your identity through the Department of Home Affairs database or through facial recognition. This is a critical block — your grant cannot proceed until your identity is successfully verified.
This status affects applicants whose identity information is being cross-checked with the Department of Home Affairs database.

contentBlocks.explanation: SASSA cross-checks every applicant's ID number, full name, and surname against the Department of Home Affairs' National Population Register. For SRD grants, an additional facial biometric verification step is required to prevent identity fraud.
whyItHappens: Your ID number does not match the name on your application (typo or data entry error)
Your ID document was reported as lost, stolen, or flagged as belonging to a deceased person
Your facial verification selfie did not match the photo on Home Affairs' database
Your biometric data was not captured clearly (poor lighting, glasses,遮挡)
Home Affairs records for your ID are outdated or contain errors
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: The block remains until you either complete facial verification or visit a SASSA office with your physical ID document. Resolving it typically takes 1 to 7 days after taking action.
whatYouShouldDo: Log into the SRD portal and check if facial verification is required
If prompted: click the secure biometric link sent to your phone and complete the selfie scan in good lighting
Ensure your face is clearly visible, remove sunglasses and masks, and follow the on-screen instructions
If facial verification fails repeatedly: visit your nearest SASSA office with your original ID document
If the issue is at Home Affairs: visit your nearest Home Affairs office to correct your ID details
whatToCheck: Check your SMS messages for an official verification link from SASSA starting with srd.sassa.gov.za.
Verify that your smartphone camera is operational and you have an internet connection.
Check that you have your physical green ID book or smart ID card ready for verification.

steps.title: Wait for the SMS link
steps.description: SASSA will send an SMS with a link starting with 'srd.sassa.gov.za'. The link is only valid for a limited time.

steps.title: Open on a smartphone
steps.description: Open the link on a smartphone with a working camera. The facial verification process is not supported on desktop computers.

steps.title: Grant camera permissions
steps.description: When prompted, allow the website to access your camera. Position your face in the centre of the frame.

steps.title: Follow the on-screen prompts
steps.description: You may be asked to blink, turn your head, or smile. Ensure good lighting and remove sunglasses, hats, or face coverings.

steps.title: Wait for confirmation
steps.description: If successful, you will see a confirmation message. Your status should update within 24 to 48 hours.

contentBlocks.text: When the Issue Is with Home Affairs

If your ID details do not match Home Affairs records, facial verification alone will not fix the problem. You need to visit a Department of Home Affairs office to correct your details. Common issues include: your ID was flagged as lost or stolen, your surname changed but was not updated, or there is a data entry error in the Home Affairs system.

contentBlocks.title: Do Not Ignore This
contentBlocks.text: If your ID is flagged as lost, stolen, or deceased, this can affect more than just your SASSA grant — it can prevent you from accessing banking, employment, and other government services. Visit Home Affairs as soon as possible.
Illustrative example: a failed selfie, twice

Facial verification failed twice for Bongani. The first attempt was taken indoors at night with a single ceiling light behind him; the second was taken wearing the glasses he had worn for years but not in his Home Affairs photograph. Neither failure said anything about his eligibility — the check compares a live image with the photograph on the population register, and poor lighting or a changed appearance makes that comparison fail.

On the third attempt he stood facing a window in daylight, removed his glasses, and held the phone steady at eye level. It passed. Only after repeated failures with a good image does the identity record itself become the suspect — and at that point the correction has to start at Home Affairs, because SASSA can only mirror what the population register says.

contentBlocks.title: Verify the link before you open it
contentBlocks.text: A genuine verification SMS points at srd.sassa.gov.za. Anyone asking you to enter an ID number, card PIN or one-time PIN on another domain is not SASSA, and no legitimate verification step ever asks for a banking password.

Home Affairs owns the identity record: the names, date of birth and photograph attached to your ID number. SASSA checks its application against that record. That division explains the order of operations — correct the Home Affairs record first at dha.gov.za or a Home Affairs office, then let SASSA re-verify. The verification requirement for the SRD grant is described on srd.sassa.gov.za.

faqs.question: How do I do facial verification for SASSA?
faqs.answer: SASSA will send an SMS with a link starting with 'srd.sassa.gov.za'. Open the link on a smartphone, grant camera permissions, and follow the on-screen prompts to scan your face.

faqs.question: I do not have a smartphone. How can I verify my identity?
faqs.answer: Visit your nearest SASSA office with your original green ID book or smart ID card. A SASSA officer can verify your identity in person.

faqs.question: Why does my ID say 'deceased' when I am alive?
faqs.answer: This is a known Home Affairs database error. Visit a Home Affairs office with your ID document to request a correction. Get a written confirmation once it is fixed.

faqs.question: Can someone else complete facial verification for me?
faqs.answer: No. Facial verification uses biometric matching against your Home Affairs photo. Only the registered applicant can complete this step.

faqs.question: I completed facial verification but my status has not changed. What now?
faqs.answer: It can take 24 to 48 hours for the verification to reflect in the SASSA system. If it has been more than 3 days, contact SASSA.
